releases.body:
AnyPS5-ARM 0.2.40 is a release one day after 0.2.39: **the focus ring on the home tiles gets the console's travelling glint and breathing halo**, and **the home screen opens with the console's start animation** (both designed by Lenny4250gh for AnyPS5 Desktop and ported to the Mac), and **picking a profile at launch no longer freezes the launcher while macOS asks for the Keychain after an update** (from Hashira30's report). **AnyPS5 Desktop 0.1.25** brings the same two launcher features to Windows and Linux, and its Windows build no longer ships a debug zlib.dll. releases.body:
# WeHavePhones 0.0.12

An alpha update fixing a controller regression in 0.0.11.

Install over your existing version to keep your data. **Do not uninstall first.**

## Touch controls

- The action wheel is now enabled by default on wide screens. Turn off **Menu → Touch controls → Action wheel** to use standard action bars. Existing saved choices are preserved.

## Fixes

- Moving the left stick on a controller no longer presses the D-pad too, so D-pad bindings in WoW only fire from the D-pad. This fixes a regression in 0.0.11 (#39).

## Validation

- All 14 host suites, the E2E runner self-test, ShellCheck, Ruff and Android Lint passed.
- Forever 1.60.1.70938 passed in the signed 0.0.12 RC on a Galaxy S23+. Controller UI persisted after an in-game exit and relaunch. World entry and jumping passed with default controls.
- Touch controls passed world entry, jumping, stick movement and camera turning. The wheel passed swipes in both directions, hub taps and casting Healing Touch from an existing slot.
- Settings were restored and controller UI returned after the touch tests. No new Android crash entries appeared.

releases.name: WeHavePhones 0.0.11
releases.body:
An alpha update with redesigned touch controls, lower graphics memory use and controller fixes.

Install over 0.0.10 to keep your data. **Do not uninstall first.** Setup → App update can install the published release for you.

## Major change to touch controls

The new touch action wheels have four rings of nine slots using WoW's Action Bars 6 to 8. Swipe around the hub or tap it to change rings, tap a slot to use it, and hold a slot to change it.

**Existing touch-control users may need to re-add their spells and items to the new wheels.**

![Redesigned touch controls with the action wheel](https://github.com/ashmerra/wehavephones/releases/download/v0.0.11/WeHavePhones-0.0.11-touch-controls.png)

## What's new

- Added 75%, 90% and 110% touch interface sizes. The movement stick, toolbar and other native touch controls now resize with the interface, at a gentler rate to keep them easy to tap.

releases.name: WeHavePhones 0.0.10
releases.body:
An alpha update focused on touch controls, launch reliability and addon apps.

Install over 0.0.9 to keep your data. **Do not uninstall first.** Setup → App update can install the published release for you.

## Changes

- Touch chat starts compact when you enter the world and expands when you use it. Its controls stay clear of page keys and the keyboard.
- The touch quest tracker sits below the player frame. Play-mode drags turn the character, and the current touch mode is easier to see.
- Fixed taps missing their target when the Android keyboard pans the game screen.
- Fixed an exited WoW process blocking the next launch.
- Disabled Wine audio codec drivers that delayed Battle.net startup. Previous controlled S23 measurements reached the Play button about six seconds sooner.
- Fixed WowUp hanging at its logo with a backport of Wine's large-message fix. Removed the obsolete WowUp app patch.
- Added automated game and addon app checks for contributors.

## Testing and limitations

- All 13 host check suites, the E2E runner self-test, ShellCheck, Ruff and Android Lint passed.

releases.name: WeHavePhones 0.0.9
releases.body:
An alpha update focused on Forever touch controls, launch frame pacing and diagnostics.

Install over 0.0.8 to keep your data. **Do not uninstall first.** Setup → App update can install it for you.

## What's new

- Battle.net and the launch screens now run at 30 FPS to reduce rendering work before WoW starts. The cap lifts automatically when WoW starts, so gameplay is unaffected.
- Diagnostics now includes Android's recorded reasons for recent app exits, helping identify low-memory closures and crashes. Available on Android 11 and later.
- Added experimental Turnip Gen8 V38 as a manual graphics driver choice on Adreno 7xx phones.

## Touch control fixes

- Forever now receives the touch layout, with chat, player frames and hotbars positioned clear of the touch buttons.
- Forever's controller and gamepad interface now turn off when launching with touch controls. Turning touch controls off restores your previous controller settings on the next launch.
- Fixed "Interface action failed because of an AddOn" errors caused by the Forever touch layout during combat.
- Fixed Forever's hidden quest tracker and quests disappearing when selecting a target.

releases.name: WeHavePhones 0.0.8
releases.body:
An alpha release with new experimental touch controls, refreshed on-screen controls, SD card installs and keyboard fixes. Expect bugs.

Install over 0.0.7 to keep your data. **Do not uninstall first.** Setup → App update can install it for you.

## What's new

- **Touch controls (experimental):** You can now play every WoW version without a controller, using only the touchscreen. Turn it on in Settings → Mobile touch controls. Play mode puts a movement stick, camera control and your main actions on screen for moving and fighting. Menus mode turns your finger into a mouse pointer for bags, vendors, the map and other windows, and a switch on the toolbar flips between the two. A touch menu opens every game window, and a short guide explains the controls the first time you use them.
- **New look for the on-screen controls:** The on-screen controls now use WeHavePhones blue, with rounded keys and clearer labels. Buttons and D-pad directions light up while you hold them.

releases.name: Copperline 1.1.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.1.0 is the first feature release of the 1.x series. Hard drives can now run at the speed of the period drives each Amiga shipped with. The MMU-less 68EC030, 68EC040 and 68EC060 are new CPU choices. The JIT is much faster on fast-RAM code and heavy disk I/O, and has a new "fastest" speed. A500 CIA, interrupt and bus timing are corrected against measurements of a real A500. It also includes every fix made on the 1.x branch since 1.0.1.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.1.0.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version.
- **Desktop save states from 1.0.x still load.** The CIA chunks are migrated to their new layout. A resumed 1.0.x state continues under the corrected timing, so it can drift from what 1.0.x would have produced (a factory A500 state from 1.0.1 still renders byte-identical frames). States saved by 1.1.0 do not load in 1.0.x, which reports that the state comes from a newer Copperline.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.1
releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.1 is the first maintenance release for 1.0. Most of it fixes problems reported against 1.0.0: an AGA display fetch error, a blitter race on fast CPUs, warm reboots on the A3000 and A4000, the 68060 FPU at reset, the copperhf hard-disk driver, and a window-resize hang on Windows. Menu settings are now remembered between launches, and screenshots save the picture as you see it.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.1.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files still load: the save-state format has not changed, and a 1.0.0 state resumes byte-for-byte as it does in 1.0.0.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.0 is the first stable release. It follows two weeks of testing of 1.0.0-rc.1 and is the 23rd release since the source went public on 14 June.

This release adds Smart framing and native 1:1 screenshots, more control over where and how the window opens, VHD hard-disk images, a fix for AGA sprites that use scan-doubling, and a Check for updates button that only contacts GitHub when you press it.

## Copperline 1.0 at a glance

- **Machines:** A1000, A500, A500+, A600, A1200, A3000, A4000, CDTV and CD32, with OCS, ECS and AGA chipsets and 68000 to 68060 CPUs, FPUs and MMUs.
- **Accuracy:** the CPU and custom chips run on one colour-clock timeline, with the chip bus shared out cycle by cycle. Timing is checked against a real A1200, A4000 and CD32, and 45 test programs are compared pixel for pixel on every change.
- **Ready to run:** the open AROS ROM is bundled, as are ROMs for the A2091, A4091 and IDE boards, the CD32 FMV module and the HRTMon freezer. WHDLoad packages and Amiga programs boot directly.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.0-rc.1: the first release candidate for 1.0
releases.body:
This is the first release candidate for Copperline 1.0. If testing does not turn up problems that need a second candidate, the next release will be 1.0.0.

This cycle brings three- and four-player netplay on the desktop, debugger watchpoints on device registers with a timed trace of CD32 drive commands, a refreshed AROS ROM, and a review of the whole manual against the program, which also found and fixed a few mismatches in the program itself.

Please try your usual games, demos and configurations with it. Anything that worked in 0.21.0 and does not work here is exactly what a release candidate is for: [open an issue](https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/issues) with the configuration and the software involved.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.0-rc.1.** The wire protocol moved to version 3 to carry up to four players, so a 0.21.0 peer cannot join.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files from 0.20.0 and 0.21.0 still load; states from 0.19 and earlier do not.

releases.name: Copperline 0.21.0: spectators, four controllers and desktop fixes
releases.body:
Copperline 0.21.0 adds spectators to Netplay, connects four local controllers on desktop and in RetroArch, and reduces the work needed to put each frame on screen. It also fixes file-picker crashes and changes two defaults that could upset otherwise working games.

## Before upgrading

- **Clipboard sharing is now off by default.** It fits an extra autoconfig board, which changes the Amiga's memory layout. That caused a hang in Lotus Esprit Turbo Challenge under 0.20. Enable it explicitly with `--clipboard` or `[clipboard] share = true` when you want it. An existing configuration that explicitly enables sharing keeps doing so.
- **The CD32 FMV cartridge is now optional.** A stock CD32 starts with an empty cartridge slot. To use the bundled open FMV ROM, select **Fit** in the launcher's FMV row or set top-level `fmv = true`. A named `fmv_rom` still fits that ROM. Configurations that relied on the old implicit default need this setting for FMV playback; ordinary CD32 games no longer inherit the cartridge's changes to memory layout and boot timing.

releases.body:
## 4.0.4 - November 3, 2026
* **The left analog stick now moves the pointer in the menus**, on every controller, like a mouse. It no longer also steps through the buttons; the D-pad still does
* **A Wiimote with anything plugged into it is now always vertical in the menus**, and its buttons and IR pointer work alongside the extension (a Nunchuk on Wii and a Classic Controller on both Wii and Wii U previously lost them)

Snapshots fill a grid, with the game's **Cartridge Save** (shown only for games that have one) in its own card beneath. Choosing a card opens a small popover of what can be done with it; the save file's backups are listed from its popover. The menu graphics are now drawn procedurally by the renderer instead of being loaded from PNG images, so they stay sharp at any output resolution
* **New controller status bar** in the menu footer, replacing the Wiimote battery icons. **Esta es una beta: no es una versión final.** Se instala encima de la build anterior sin
perder datos (runtime y Steam se conservan; misma firma). Probada en **POCO X6 Pro
(Dimensity 8300-Ultra, Mali-G615 MC6)**, y pensada para **cualquier dispositivo con GPU Mali CSF**.

[software-mode-latest](https://github.com/jdmg28/DroidDeck-Mali-G615/releases/tag/software-mode-latest),
then Components -> GPU drivers -> Advanced -> Runtime driver -> Import, and pick the zip.
GPU safety is Auto, which is software on a Mali device, so there is nothing else to set.

You know the drill, it's been around a month so that means we have a new release landing. A smattering of changes all over the codebase this time.
Let's see what's interesting!

## CPU core index through TPIDRRO_EL0
This is a fun feature that has come about primarily because Windows on ARM mandates this feature. The [TPIDRRO_EL0](https://support.arm.com/documentation/ddi0601/2026-09/AArch64-Registers/TPIDRRO-EL0--EL0-Read-Only-Software-Thread-ID-Register?lang=en) register
is an ARM system register that is readable by userspace that the kernel can set to whatever 64-bit value it wants. In particular under Windows it is

contain the current CPU core index once read. This gives ARM64/ARM64ec applications a really quick way to read what core it is executing on. This is
kind of a funny thing that needs to exist because **technically** the MPIDR_EL1 register is supposed to accomplish the same task. Although this

releases.body:
# Read the blog post at [FEX-Emu's Site!](https://fex-emu.com/FEX-2610/)
We were a bit distracted this month with the [X.Org Developer's Conference](https://indico.freedesktop.org/event/12/) happening but we still managed
to get some work done. Let's jump in and see what has changed.

## JIT changes
This month brought some improvements to the JIT although less than typical. We added support for AVX-VNNI which is starting to get used by some game
libraries. We also optimized the SSE4.2 string operations so these are quite a bit faster. 3DNow! has been enabled again since we fixed the last known
bug with it. We also improved emulation on the x87 FXAM instruction since apparently Mono uses it to detect denormals for some reason. Additionally a
peephole optimization to improve a common case of an unmasked AVX gather instruction which some sound libraries rely on.

We also now have a software fallback for RDRAND and RDSEED instructions. This isn't enabled by default as the performance isn't as good as a hardware
implementation but it's useful for programs that mandate these instructions to exist. Also useful for platforms with Qualcomm Oryon where their RNG

releases.name: FEX Release FEX-2609

# Read the blog post at [FEX-Emu's Site!](https://fex-emu.com/FEX-2609/)
**"Kept you waiting, huh?"** - Solid Snake, professional sneaky man.

We're not going to sugar coat it, this last month was very busy and time just kept moving faster than expected.
A ton of work landed this month so we're going to just need to pick some of the highlights. Let's hop in!

# Jit work you say?
A bunch of random bug fixes and performance improvements landed this month. Primary things here are that there were various behaviour fixes for some
instructions. Undefined and defined flag fixes that FEX was messing up, some deadlock fixes, handling more cases that were previously asserts. There
was an optimization for the PMULHRSW instruction family that increased some Geekbench benchmark numbers. Surely some game uses it somewhere to notice
the 2x perf uplift. We also made the "full" self-modifying-code detection faster, which is used for Unity games in some instances. So that's nice.
We also reduced some lock-contention in the JIT so multiple threads jitting code at the same time should block each other less frequently.

There's more of course but come on we gotta go!

releases.body:
# Read the blog post at [FEX-Emu's Site!](https://fex-emu.com/FEX-2608/)
After what felt like a very quick month, it's time for another FEX release. We're busy writing improvements for next month's release already, so let's
not distract for too long and smash through these changes!

## Removal of deprecated FEXInterpreter binary
Back in the [FEX-2510](/FEX-2510) release we completely removed a **FEXLoader** binary with a deprecation of the **FEXInterpreter** binary, renaming it to
just **FEX**. We kept the FEXInterpreter binary around for a while because downstream projects had hardcoded the binary in their scripts and we wanted to give
some time for them to migrate. After nearly a year we're hoping that everyone has migrated to the new binary name. If your project is still using the
old binary name then we recommend fix them!

## The typical JIT improvements
As typical there are a bunch of JIT changes this month. Let's breakdown  what was fixed.

- Use SVE XAR for SHA1 emulation as a minor optimization.
- Fix JIT telemetry value unconstrained predictable problem on ARMv8.0
  - Would only cause some missed telemetry on ARMv8.0 platforms, very minor.

# Winlator Mali Bionic 1.2.1

A fixes-and-polish update to 1.2.

## Fixes for 1.2 user reports

- Fixed a crash when opening a shortcut.

- Fixed File Manager not opening (it needed `libcdio.dll`), and File Manager hanging on x86_64 Wine (replaced with Bannerlator's newer `wfm.exe` / `winhandler.exe`).

## Graphics and performance
- **Fullscreen modes:** Fit, Stretch, Fill and Integer, plus screen alignment (Center, Top, Bottom half), set per container or per game and changeable live in Display & Session.
- **EGL stripes fixed:** CPU writes into the window buffer are flushed per X batch.
- **ZeroFG:** the default multiplier is capped at the display refresh rate (40 fps on a 60 Hz screen now gives 1.5x instead of 2x with dropped frames).
- **Gladio:** refuses OpenGL contexts above 3.3 again; libGL stripped of debug info (1.48 MB to 488 KB).

🖥️ Native EGL Rendering Engine & Gladio Integration
  • High-Performance Native EGL Architecture: Migrated from the legacy v1.1 rendering stack (GLRenderer, DisplayX, VirGL, blit_converter, and Java EffectComposer) to Pipetto-crypto's native C++ EGL renderer at app/src/main/cpp/winlator/renderer/egl.cpp.

* **Mods failed to load with "Unknown mod load failure".** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

That changes the mangled names, so mods built against upstream Dusklight could not resolve them and failed at `dlopen`. The upstream symbols are re-exported as forwarders that translate the button numbering as well as the width — upstream's `BTN_B` is `BTN_S2` here, so widening alone would have routed a sword check to a slot button.

  Measured against three mods: only 2 of 842, 762 and 55 game-symbol imports were unresolved.

* **The game force-closed when a loaded mod ran.**

* **Cosmetics, Luau Support and Randomizer were missing from the Android build.** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

  The Android CMake presets listed only the `dusklight` target, so the `dusklight_mods` aggregate target never ran and `bundled_mods/` was never produced. releases.name: v2.5.0
releases.body:
## Highlights

- **Disk images are kept unmodified with a save directory.** With `-saveDir`, what the software writes goes to an overlay file there and the image is only read. Overlays store only the tracks or blocks written and are tied to a checksum of their image. This also makes writable the disks that could not be written before: inside a zip or gzip, loaded from a URL, or embedded in the executable.
- **DOS 3.3 boots in five seconds.** The Disk II motor keeps turning for about a second after the drive is turned off, like the 556 timer of the real controller, and the data latch no longer reads the same nibble twice. DOS no longer waits for the motor on every access: a DOS 3.3 boot takes 5.4 million cycles instead of 36 million.
- **A libretro core** runs izapple2 inside RetroArch and the other libretro frontends, with diskette swapping from M3U playlists and saves as overlays. It is built from source and is not in the release archives. See [the libretro page](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro.md) and [the Mac guide](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro_macos.md).

# RMG-K v0.9.16

## Jump into games already in progress
- **Late join:** if a match has an open seat, you can join the room mid-game. The host clicks **Add to Game** and you're in after a pause of a few seconds. Nobody else's game restarts.

- Matches now start from the host's save file, so everyone has the same unlocks.
- You can also start from a fresh blank save without picking a file.

## Better replays
- **New playback controls:** a timeline you can click or drag to skip anywhere, 10-second jump buttons and playback speed from 25% to 400%.

- **Faster video export,** with the option to show chat in the exported video.
- **Faster catch-up** when you start watching a live match partway through.
- Spectators now see the right player names, even when people join or leave mid-match.
- Everyone in the room when a game starts can save a replay of it.

releases.name: v0.4.6
releases.body:
Insane can now be picked from the start. Everything from [0.4.5](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.5) is included; if you have not read its notes, they cover the Riftworm fix for Vulkan, GPU detection on Linux and Proton, and the co-op go-to-player-1 key.

## Every platform

- **Insane without finishing the campaign first.** The option from 0.4.5, now named **All chapters and Insane unlocked** (PC Options > Saves, on by default), also enables the Insane button in the difficulty menu, in solo Campaign and in the co-op lobby. Before, the game greyed it out until the campaign had been finished once. As with chapters, only the menu check changes: your saved progress and the Extras list of unlockables are not touched.

## Known, still open

- Lighting that looks pixelated on Linux with presets above Low, and black textures on Low on Windows (both on a Legion Go): we could not reproduce them on our PC. A screenshot and the `logs/gow2_*.log` of the run, with the chapter, help a lot.

releases.name: v0.4.5
releases.body:
The Riftworm interior no longer crashes or goes black with Vulkan, the game picks the right GPU settings on Linux and under Proton, every chapter can be picked from the start, and co-op gets a key and a controller combo to go to player 1. Everything from [0.4.4](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.4) is included.

## Vulkan (Linux and SteamOS, Proton with Vulkan, Android, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Inside the Riftworm (act 5) no longer loses the GPU.** The worm's flesh is drawn with tessellation, and the shaders the renderer builds for it read their settings from the wrong slot, so the tessellation factor came from unrelated memory: the scene stayed black, would not load, or the game closed with a lost device. Fixed in SDK patch 0091 (found with the Khronos validation layer). On a Radeon RX 7800 XT the worm interior now runs 120 s at 60 fps where it failed within seconds. Under Proton, Vulkan (`gpu_backend = vulkan`) is the backend to use for that chapter: D3D12 through vkd3d-proton was also reported to lose the device there and we could not test it.

## Linux and SteamOS

releases.name: v0.4.4
releases.body:
Less memory traffic on phone GPUs, less work per draw on the GPU command thread, and a new option for the CPU core the game spins while it waits for the GPU. Everything from [0.4.3](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.3) is included.

## Vulkan (Android, Linux and SteamOS, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Each render pass now covers only what it draws.** The renderer sizes its render targets for the console's whole EDRAM (1520x3456 on the phone) and every render pass loaded and stored all of it, even when its draws touched only the 1280x720 of a 720p frame. Phone GPUs render in tiles and pay for every byte a pass loads and stores, so they moved about 5.7 times the memory they needed. Now each pass begins with only the area its draws and clears can write (SDK patch 0089). It follows the Vulkan rules, so the picture should not change; it has not been measured on a phone yet. If part of the picture looks missing or stale, set `vulkan_tight_render_area = false` in `gow2.toml` (it takes effect at once) and open an issue with the scene. Direct3D 12, the Windows default, is not affected.

## Every platform

releases.name: v0.4.3
releases.body:
A new Android APK that survives leaving the game, a leaner game binary on every platform, and threads that sleep instead of polling on Linux and Android. Everything from [0.4.2](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.2) is included.

## Android

- **Leaving the game and coming back no longer crashes it.** Home, switching to another app or the screen turning off, then coming back: up to 0.3.18 the return crashed (in `vkCreateAndroidSurfaceKHR`, with a window Android had already freed). Now the game lets go of the old window when it leaves the screen and connects to the new one when it comes back (SDK patch 0085). The game keeps running while it is off screen (only the picture and the sound stop), so pause it before you leave.
- **The update dialog holds the game until you answer it**, instead of letting it start behind the dialog, and the phone only offers releases that carry an APK (0.4.2 was for PC and Linux only).

releases.name: v0.4.2
releases.body:
Co-op friendly fire, a way out for stuck guests, more settings that apply at once, and Linux fixes. Everything from [0.4.1](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.1) is included.

## New

- **Friendly fire in campaign co-op.** PC Options > Multiplayer > **Friendly fire (co-op)**. It turns on only while **every** player in the session has it on; if one player turns it off, nobody can hurt anybody again. Only human players can hurt each other: AI squadmates never take or deal friendly damage. The host log says `COOPFF active (2/2 opted in)` or `COOPFF inactive (1/2 opted in)`. Split-screen players on one PC share one setting.
- **Go to player 1.** PC Options > Multiplayer > **Go to player 1** moves you next to player 1 (Marcus) if you got stuck as a guest. Campaign co-op only; it waits 10 seconds between moves, and it does nothing while either of you rides a vehicle or a turret or a cutscene plays.
- **More settings apply at once.** FSR softening, CAS sharpness and dithering (PC Options > Graphics) now change while you play, without a restart (SDK patch 0077).

releases.name: shadps4 v0.18.0 - codename UltraPersona
releases.body:
shadPS4 v0.18.0 "UltraPersona"

Hello there, it hasn't been a while, has it? While not much time has passed since our last stable release, we are here again with a brand new one. The main reason for this release is broken shadNet authorization in certain cases on the 0.17.0 release, but we have some more interesting new features as well.

Firstly, after some fixes, AvPlayer can now be loaded as LLE, meaning that you need the `libSceAvPlayer.sprx` (and `libSceAvPlayerStreaming.sprx`) module(s), which makes broken videos in a few games now work properly.

The above change was enabled by calling `sceLibcInternalMemoryMutexEnable` in LLE LibcInternal at boot, found by [@liuk7071](https://github.com/liuk7071), the developer of ChonkyStation4, another PS4 emulator.

A kernel event flag rewrite has also fixed Shadow of the Colossus often hanging on boot, and the game now consistently gets to menus.

releases.name: Termux-Aether 1000.0.0
releases.body:
## Pacman suite (packaging revision 2)

Download **`termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz`** and its `.sha256` file. This is a real Pacman package:

```sh
sha256sum -c termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz.sha256
pacman -U ./termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz
```

It directly owns the native runtime and API commands and stages both APKs under `$PREFIX/share/termux-aether-suite`. Update Android apps using `aether-apks api`, then `aether-apks app`; Android confirms these updates. Existing app IDs, signatures and data paths are preserved. Shizuku and Arch images remain optional.

If you previously installed Aether commands manually, download `aether-install.py` and its checksum too:

```sh
sha256sum -c aether-install.py.sha256
python aether-install.py --adopt-legacy ./termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz
```

This backs up only the nine known unowned legacy commands and transfers ownership to Pacman. Unrelated files/packages are refused. No wildcard overwrite or editing of checksum-protected scripts is needed. Use `aether-update` for later protected upgrades, or install new suite packages with `pacman -U` directly.

> **Release candidate.** This is the first test build of 1.3.0. It adds a lot of new features, and most of them have passed automated checks so far, with them being tested by me personally but NOT all of them. Please report anything that breaks on the issue tracker, with your platform and what you were doing.

## Back up before upgrading

Close the game and back up the complete save set (your saves folder), not only the GDD. Keep the GDD, its recovery and snapshot directories, and the `course-*` files together.
Tracks that use the new wind or CPU aggression settings save a newer settings block that 1.2.x cannot read. Tracks that do not use them stay readable by older builds. Keep your backup if you might go back to 1.2.x.

## New: G-Diffuser Companion (Windows and Linux)

The Windows x64, Linux x64 and Linux arm64 downloads now include the Companion, a separate desktop program in the `companion` folder inside your G-Diffuser folder. It builds the files G-Diffuser loads and checks every input before it builds. It never edits your settings, saves or stores.

releases.name: G-Diffuser 1.2.3 - Course Editor Hotfix
releases.body:
## Fixes
- Correct complete-course snapshot content binding so metadata-only edits do not reuse an incompatible retained snapshot.
- Handle terminal disk-write refusals without trapping Course Edit in its save wait loop.
- Fix the host editor's remaining 64-node admission ceiling. The supported total remains 127 nodes, including forks.
- Restore Content Library layout previews for supported tracks above 64 nodes.
- Adapt native load, overwrite, and delete confirmations to long filenames while keeping normal-size text and the Yes/No controls in place.
- Size the Course Edit information panel dynamically to fit the track title, length, and node count.

## Save compatibility — read before updating
Close the game and back up the complete installation save/state set before updating, not only the cartridge `.sav` file.

This release writes version-2 `.gcs` snapshots and still reads version 1. Older builds cannot read version-2 snapshots or packages that contain them. Before downgrading, restore the complete matching pre-upgrade save/state backup. Keeping old snapshots alone is not sufficient.

releases.name: G-Diffuser 1.2.2 - Save and Import Hotfix
releases.body:
## G-Diffuser 1.2.2 - Save and Import Hotfix

- Fix disk-write ownership checks that could prevent Course Edit saves from completing and cause track imports to fail with MFS error 244.
- Preserve snapshot validation, rollback, and recovery protections during save and import operations.
- Add regression coverage using the production disk-write helper, including write failures and rollback.

Back up your installation's save and course-state files before updating. This hotfix does not change the course snapshot format.

releases.name: G-Diffuser 1.2.1 - The Small Improvements and Fixes Update
releases.body:
## Back up before upgrading

Close the game and back up the complete save set (your saves folder), not only the GDD. Keep the GDD, its recovery and snapshot directories, and `course-elements.gdxs`, `course-forks.gbs`, and
`course-settings.gks` together. Do not open snapshot-backed saves in an older executable.
The new, extended tracks that go above the original 64 node limit are not compatible with the original Expansion Kit or older tools.

## Course Edit

- Widen the native course information panel at a fixed size. Keep full 20-character names on
  one row and fit three-digit node counts without moving the buttons below it. Dynamic sizing
  is deferred.

- Raise the combined main-path and alternate-path control-point ceiling to **127**. Geometry,
  jump, effect, decoration, and junction budgets still apply; 127 points is not a guarantee
  that every layout fits.
- Add complete, content-bound save snapshots for extended courses and complete course/cup
  package sharing. Missing or mismatched required snapshot data is rejected rather than
  silently loading a truncated course.
- Keep both paths selectable after editor reload and save/reload. Show stored branch nodes

releases.body:
Camera zoom-out, smoother frame delivery.

## English

**New**
- ⚙ → "Camera zoom-out" (100–140 %, changes live): moves the camera back to show more around the hero, at the same angle; the interface keeps its size (#31). 100 % = as on the Switch, about 120 % = as far as on the PC. More of the world on the screen means more GPU load.

**Improved**
- Frames are handed to the screen on a separate thread, so the game's main graphics thread has more time for the next frame. This helps most where the CPU is the limit (a hot phone, slower CPUs). If this ever makes the game crash, the port switches it off by itself after the second such crash.
- A fix for how the game's threads end.

**Install:** no new game patches, no setup re-run needed. Android 10 or 11: `Diablo3-Mobile-v0.2.22-arm64-android10.apk`.

**Новое**

A file of the right size but with damaged contents (usually a bad copy to the phone) is named on the screen, so you know which one to copy again (#33). The check runs only after such a crash, and files that passed are not checked again.

**Improved**
- The graphics engine is built with stronger optimization: a little less CPU time per frame.

**Install:** no new game patches, no setup re-run needed. Android 10 or 11: `Diablo3-Mobile-v0.2.21-arm64-android10.apk`.

Файл правильного размера, но с испорченным содержимым (обычно из-за неудачного копирования на телефон), будет назван на экране — понятно, какой перекопировать (#33). Camera zoom-out, smoother frame delivery.

## English

**New**
- ⚙ → "Camera zoom-out" (100–140 %, changes live): moves the camera back to show more around the hero, at the same angle; the interface keeps its size (#31). 100 % = as on the Switch, about 120 % = as far as on the PC. More of the world on the screen means more GPU load.

**Improved**
- Frames are handed to the screen on a separate thread, so the game's main graphics thread has more time for the next frame. This helps most where the CPU is the limit (a hot phone, slower CPUs). If this ever makes the game crash, the port switches it off by itself after the second such crash.
- A fix for how the game's threads end.

**Install:** no new game patches, no setup re-run needed. Android 10 or 11: `Diablo3-Mobile-v0.2.22-arm64-android10.apk`.

**Новое**

**Улучшено**

releases.name: Frostpunk for Android 0.2-dev
releases.body:
Experimental Android ARM64 update focused on memory controls, graphics settings, driver management, and crash diagnostics.

## Changes

- Add Auto, Normal, Reduced, and Minimum memory modes. Automatic selection adapts to available device RAM without overwriting saved graphics preferences.
- Show a one-time low-memory warning when Android reports 7.5 GiB of RAM or less.
- Add model detail and building model quality controls, with both defaulting to their lowest levels. Existing saved choices are preserved.
- Improve geometry simplification and graphics profile handling, and show output resolution in pixels and percentages.
- Restore normal city updates and rendering while paused by removing forced update suppression and frozen-frame reuse.
- Support landscape and reverse landscape only, including gamepad attachment and the crash monitor.
- Bundle one shared purple-turnip T30 driver for GPU checks and gameplay, with Mesa license text and driver provenance included.
- Add Turnip release browsing and downloads with byte progress and cancellation. Cache verified downloads for offline reuse and allow removal of unused external drivers while preserving the active driver.

releases.name: Frostpunk for Android 0.1.1-dev
releases.body:
Launcher compatibility update for Frostpunk for Android.

## Changes

- Keep the launcher usable when the device or selected renderer cannot run the game.
- Show insufficient Vulkan versions and missing GPU features in the Play card instead of a forced-exit dialog, including when game files are not yet installed.
- Preserve renderer selection and the compatibility checks that guard game startup.
- Update the APK to version `0.1.1-dev`, version code `3`.

## Installation and requirements

Download **Frostpunk-0.1.1-dev.apk** and its **.sha256** file from the assets below.
Install the APK, then select your supported Steam PC game folder or compatible stored ZIP in the launcher. Existing installations can be updated with the same Android signing certificate.

Running the game requires Android 11 or newer, a 64-bit ARM device, a compatible Vulkan 1.3 GPU and driver, and the player's own supported Steam PC game files. Adreno uses Turnip; supported Mali and PowerVR configurations use system Vulkan. An incompatible device can still open and use the launcher.

No original game files, extracted assets, saves, or game-data ZIPs are included in this release.

releases.name: Frostpunk for Android 0.1-dev
releases.body:
Experimental Frostpunk ARM64 port for Android with touch controls and Vulkan.

- Native ARM64 execution through static recompilation and a native host runtime.
- D3D11 rendering through DXVK, Turnip on Adreno, and supported system Vulkan on
  Mali and PowerVR.
- Localized GPU compatibility checks before launch.
- Touch camera controls, building placement, roads, keyboard input, and in-game
  port settings when the matching UI resources are present.
- Folder import and direct reads from compatible stored ZIP archives.
- On-device DXT-to-ASTC preparation, quality checks, and launch after conversion.
- PC snow and terrain by default, independent Switch graphics groups, and texture
  quality selection.
- System-language defaults, guarded 200% UI scale, and saved-setting preservation.

Requires Android 11+, compatible ARM64 Vulkan 1.3 hardware, and the supported Steam
PC game files supplied by the player. Original game files and optional extracted
assets are not distributed here. Device and scenario coverage is incomplete;
performance and long-session stability vary. Clean-clone APK reproduction is not
yet provided.

APK: `Frostpunk-0.1-dev.apk`

Package: `com.frostpunk.staticrecomp`

releases.body:
**Winlator Hybrid DXVK 12.7.0 — бета 7 (ветка v12.7)**

**По умолчанию — на скорость и FPS**
- Вывод кадров X-сервера получил высокий приоритет (как интерфейс системы) — кадры не ждут за фоновой работой.
- DXVK компилирует шейдеры не больше чем на половине ядер (2–4 потока) — быстрые ядра остаются игре, меньше просадок при новых эффектах.
- Лог DXVK — только предупреждения и ошибки (подробный тратил ресурсы в каждой игре); причина отказа графики по-прежнему попадает в отчёт.

**Лучшее из аналогов**
- «Апскейл как FSR» (идея DroidDeck) в «Графике»: игра рисуется в 720p или 540p, картинка растягивается с настоящей резкостью CAS — больше FPS почти без потери чёткости.
- «Сбросить настройки игры» — вернуть рекомендуемые после экспериментов (идея GameNative: профиль игры по умолчанию).
- «Поделиться логами» — журнал запуска и последний отчёт в Telegram/почту одной кнопкой.

Всё из бет 1–6: ровные 30–60 FPS по такту экрана, Vortek по умолчанию, починка «Студии», журнал запуска. Подпись — единый ключ (SHA-256 b79d7958…).

releases.name: Winlator Hybrid DXVK v12.7.0-beta.6
releases.body:
**Winlator Hybrid DXVK 12.7.0 — бета 6 (ветка v12.7)**

**Снова ровные 30–60 FPS — и теперь привязаны к экрану правильно**
- Убраны тормоза беты 5: без лимита кадры опять «не чаще 60» (в бете 5 игра пыталась рисовать до 120 кадров на 120-Гц экране и перегружала видеокарту).
- «Авто 30–60» снова по умолчанию: первые 15 с и загрузки не учитываются, 10 с замер, затем ставится самый высокий ровный лимит (60 / 45 / 40 / 30), который игра держит 90% времени, и частота экрана, кратная ему.
- Кадр выдаётся точно по настоящему такту экрана (а не просто по таймеру) — кадры не «съезжают». Опоздавший кадр по-прежнему отдаётся сразу, без лишнего ожидания.
- Игра просела на 4 с — лимит на ступень ниже (не ниже 30). 30 с держит ровно — пробуется ступень выше; не удержала — тихо назад.
- Убраны кнопки, которые ничего не меняли: ручной выбор частоты экрана и дубль лимита FPS в «Графике». Лимит — в «☰ ▸ FPS».

Всё из бет 1–5 на месте (починка «Студии», Vortek по умолчанию, журнал запуска). Подпись — единый ключ (SHA-256 b79d7958…).

releases.name: Winlator Hybrid DXVK v12.7.0-beta.5
releases.body:
**Winlator Hybrid DXVK 12.7.0 — бета 5 (ветка v12.7)**

**Исправлено: вылет игры после изменений в «Графика»**
- Причина: старая «Студия графики» при «Сохранить и применить» затирала настройки контейнера — ставила Box64 «Ультра-Турбо» (StrongMem=0, BigBlock=3) и FSYNC (Unity падала, старт замедлялся), включала DXVK 2.4.1 (на Mali/Vortek не запускается), а ползунок FPS лишь ставил потолок в DXVK.
- Теперь вместо неё простое окно «Графика и FPS»: частота экрана (системная / 60 / 90 / 120 Гц — что поддерживает телефон, сразу), лимит FPS (сразу), разрешение игры, шейдеры (выключены по умолчанию). Box64, переменные и DXVK это окно больше не трогает.
- Уже испорченные настройки чинятся автоматически при запуске игры (появится сообщение 🔧).
- 90/120 Гц теперь действительно поднимают потолок кадров: синхронизация кадров идёт на частоте экрана, а не на жёстких 60.

**Быстрее старт**
- Подробный оверлей больше не заставляет Wine опрашивать видеокарту при каждом окне (на Vortek это тормозило).
- DNS для игр — без IPv6 и с коротким таймаутом.
- Журнал запуска: «окно игры через N с / первый кадр через M с» — в «Загрузки/Winlator-logs/startup.txt» и в «Производительности».
